_why: Ruled build steps that own a FAMILY of recurring alerts, and which census types each one prevents. Founded 2026-10-02 (design/PLAN-weekly-root-families-2026-10-02.md Phase 1, Brad's ruling D3 A): steps 8, 9 and 11 were ruled 2026-09-10 and sat unbuilt for 22 days while triage paid for their symptoms one at a time. Read by grocery/ruled-step-lib.ps1: grocery/audit-alert-census.ps1 prints each step's attributed alerts over 14 days and pages a ruled step that is not under way 14 days after its ruling, and grocery/validate-triage-plan.ps1 accepts a residual owner 'step:<ref>' only for a step listed here or any step of a plan whose Status reads RULED or under way.

_fields.ref: <repo-relative plan>#<label>. The label is the step heading's text up to its first '.' or ':', lower-cased, spaces as hyphens: '### 8. Ruling 2' is '8', '### Phase 5. Chain data flow' is 'phase-5', '### Stage 2: enforce' is 'stage-2'.
_fields.ruled: the date Brad ruled the step (YYYY-MM-DD). The 14-day stall clock runs from it.
_fields.under_way_evidence: repo-relative files whose existence means the build has started (the files the step creates first). Empty means nothing can show it started, so the step reads NOT under way.
_fields.type_prefixes: census type keys (grocery/out/alert-census.jsonl 'type') this step prevents, matched as a prefix. A type belongs to ONE step: the one whose landing stops the ALERT. Review-class types go to step 11 (the packet adjudicates them) even where the defect they report is a family 1 or 2 root.
_fields.finished: a step is finished when its plan heading carries '[DONE' (e.g. '### 8. Ruling 2, the row contract [DONE 2026-11-01]'). A bare 'DONE' does not count, because 3b's heading reads 'TRIAL DONE, NOT BUILT'.
